entry.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
entry.rationale: The primary objective is to identify Mauro Cruz Corona's parents. Civil birth registrations (actas de nacimiento) and Catholic baptismal records for Michoacán in this era routinely name both parents, making this the highest-priority question. Nueva Italia was a planned agricultural colony founded in the Tierra Caliente region of Michoacán around 1903, so records from surrounding parishes and the civil registry of Parácuaro or Gabriel Zamora are the most likely repositories. Answering parentage is the central goal and will likely resolve the birth date/place sub-question simultaneously.

quirks: Nueva Italia de Ruiz was founded c. 1903 and remained part of Parácuaro municipality until Múgica was created on February 12, 1942. All civil registration and church records for Nueva Italia before 1942 are filed under Parácuaro — never search 'Múgica' for pre-1942 events.

FamilySearch wiki explicitly states no records are available online for Múgica municipality (civil registration, church records, or census). Research must target Parácuaro, the predecessor jurisdiction.

FamilySearch has 193 digitized Parácuaro civil registration volumes (marriages 1881–1930 and deaths 1881–1930 fully indexed; birth volumes visible from 1917 in first-page results). Birth records for 1910–1916 may be absent or in later volume-search pages — the full 193-volume set must be checked via the indexed CID 1916243 collection search.
Several Parácuaro Nacimientos (birth) volumes for 1926–1930 have 0 images — digitized but not yet scanned; not accessible online.

Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) and Cristero War (1926–1929) disrupted civil registration in Tierra Caliente. Gaps in civil records for these periods are expected; church baptismal records are the fallback.

The Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records collection (CID 1883388) covers approximately 1549–1909 per the collection wiki page. Baptisms in this collection include date/place of birth, parents' names, and godparents — essential for pre-1910 parentage research.

Nueva Italia was a new colony in 1903 with no dedicated parish; residents used the nearest established Catholic parishes, most likely in Parácuaro or Apatzingán. Browse both when searching parish registers.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz (Parácuaro), Michoacán, Mexico (1880–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- Nueva Italia de Ruiz was founded c. 1903 as a planned agricultural colony (hacienda Cusi lands) in the Tierra Caliente region of Michoacán.
- Modern municipality: Múgica (created Feb 12, 1942). In 1910, the jurisdiction was **Parácuaro municipality** (est. 1861).
- All civil registration and church records for Nueva Italia before 1942 were filed under Parácuaro.
- Catholic archdiocese: Arquidiócesis de Morelia.

## Critical jurisdictional note
FamilySearch wiki states explicitly: 'There are no records available online for the municipality of Múgica.' Research must target Parácuaro.

## Available record types

### Civil registration (Parácuaro)
- CID 1916243: Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940 — indexed + images at FamilySearch
- 193 digitized Parácuaro volumes confirmed: marriages 1881–1930 and deaths 1881–1930 (all 100% indexed). Birth volumes visible from 1917; 1910–1916 may be absent or in later search pages.
- Ancestry parallel: Michoacan Civil Registration Births 1859–1934 ($)

### Church records
- CID 1883388: Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996 (wiki states coverage c. 1549–1909) — index only; browse by parish
- Baptism records include: date/place of birth, parents' names, godparents
- No dedicated Nueva Italia parish existed in 1910; use Parácuaro and Apatzingán parishes

### Census
- 1930 National Census (CID 1307314) — indexed + images; key resource for locating Mauro c. age 20

### Border crossings
- US Border Crossings from Mexico 1903–1957 (CID 1803932)

## Research tips
1. Search 'Parácuaro' not 'Nueva Italia' or 'Múgica' in civil registration.
2. Start with indexed CID 1916243 collection search by surname.
3. For parentage: search parents' marriage record in Parácuaro Matrimonios (indexed 1881–1930).
4. For pre-1910 baptisms: use CID 1883388; browse Parácuaro and Apatzingán parishes.
5. Search the 1930 census for Mauro and household.
6. If not found: try neighboring parishes (Apatzingán, La Huacana, Churumuco).
7. Revolution-era gaps (1910–1920): use church baptismal records when civil records are missing.

Parácuaro municipality (est. 1861) was the registering jurisdiction for Nueva Italia before Múgica was created in 1942. Search CID 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940) — fully indexed — for Mauro Cruz Corona. Mexican naming convention confirms the paternal surname is Cruz and the maternal surname is Corona; the birth record (acta de nacimiento) would name both parents. The locality survey (loc_001) found no Parácuaro birth volumes online for 1910–1916 specifically, so also check the indexed collection for records that may not appear in individual volume searches. Try Cruz, Cruces, and Corona spelling variants.

Catholic baptismal records are the primary fallback when civil birth registration is absent or shows a gap — the locality survey (loc_001) flagged that Parácuaro civil birth volumes for 1910–1916 may not be in the digitized set, and the Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration in Tierra Caliente. Search CID 1883388 (Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996), browsing by parish via Parácuaro and the nearest larger parish, Apatzingán. Also search Mexico Baptisms 1560–1950 (CID 1473011). Baptism records name the child's parents, godparents, legitimacy, and birth date — providing direct parentage evidence. entry.rationale: The 1930 Mexico National Census (CID 1307314) is fully indexed and is the only available national census for this period accessible online. Mauro Cruz Corona, born c. 1910, would be approximately 20 years old in 1930 — potentially still in the parental household in Nueva Italia, or at least enumerated nearby. The census can confirm exact birth year, birth place (municipio), and relationship to head of household. If parents were still living, the household listing would directly name them. Also check at Ancestry (1930 Mexico National Census). This is an independent record type from the civil/church birth series and should be searched regardless of outcome at step 1.

A dedicated search for the parents' marriage record is required for every parentage plan. Mexican naming convention indicates Mauro's father carried Cruz as his first (paternal) surname and his mother carried Corona as her first (paternal) surname. A civil marriage record between a Cruz man and a Corona woman registered in Parácuaro c. 1890–1912 (allowing time before Mauro's ~1910 birth) would: (a) confirm the couple as a married unit; (b) supply the mother's full compound surname (her maiden name) and the father's full name; (c) by its date before Mauro's birth, corroborate that this couple could be his parents. Note: the marriage record alone does not prove Mauro is their child — that requires a birth record placing him with them. Search CID 1916243 (civil registration) and Mexico Marriages 1570–1950 (CID 1473012) for Cruz × Corona marriage in Parácuaro.

Church marriage records (informaciones matrimoniales and actas de matrimonio) are the fallback when civil marriage registration is missing. The locality survey confirmed that Parácuaro Matrimonios volumes at FamilySearch are 100% indexed for 1881–1930. Search CID 1883388 (Catholic Church Records) browsing Parácuaro parish marriage registers for a Cruz × Corona marriage. The window is sized for the parents' likely union (1890–1910, covering 20 years before Mauro's birth c. 1910). The Arquidiócesis de Morelia marriage information volumes (Información matrimonial) are also indexed for many years — include those.

FAN item — required for a parentage question (BCG Standard 14). Three siblings are already in the tree: Miguel Cruz, Liborio Cruz, and Facundo Cruz (full names likely Cruz Corona). Their birth or baptism records, filed in the same Parácuaro civil registry or parish, would independently name the same parents as Mauro, providing corroborating parentage evidence. Search CID 1916243 for Cruz Corona births and CID 1883388 for Cruz baptisms in Parácuaro, 1895–1925 (sized to cover likely sibling birth years: if Mauro was born ~1910, siblings could be born from the mid-1890s to the mid-1920s). The window's upper bound is governed by the siblings' plausible birth years relative to the parents, not Mauro's. A sibling's record naming both parents provides independent corroboration for the parentage conclusion.

Full-text co-occurrence search for surnames Cruz and Corona in FamilySearch Catholic records — execute via search-full-text skill, not search-records. Per the record-type guide, for a compound Iberian surname (Cruz = paternal, Corona = maternal), a full-text search requiring both surnames as co-occurring terms is the highest-yield tactic when indexed search stalls. This surfaces Mauro's baptism entry, a parent's burial or marriage act, or a sibling's record from registers that are digitized but incompletely indexed. The search is unscoped (not restricted to a single collection id) to catch records across all Michoacán volumes. Use both 'Cruz' and 'Corona' as required terms, not as a phrase, since clerks sometimes reverse or conflate the paternal/maternal order. This item complements steps 1–2; execute it when those return insufficient results.

Ancestry hosts Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births 1859–1934 as a separate indexed collection with images — a different index and imaging pipeline from FamilySearch's CID 1916243. A subject not found in FamilySearch may appear here due to different name standardization, OCR, or coverage. Search for Mauro Cruz Corona and spelling variants. This is a paid ($) resource. Execute as a fallback when FamilySearch civil registration (step 1) returns nothing.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz (Parácuaro), Michoacán, Mexico (1880–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Place of interest:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz — founded c. 1903 as a private agricultural colony (hacienda Cusi lands) in the Tierra Caliente region
- **Modern municipality:** Múgica, Michoacán — **created February 12, 1942**
- **Predecessor jurisdiction (1880–1942):** Parácuaro municipality (est. 1861); Parácuaro is the civil registry unit that would have registered births, marriages, and deaths for Nueva Italia in 1910
- **Administrative center:** Parácuaro (municipal seat); Morelia (state capital)
- **Catholic archdiocese:** Arquidiócesis de Morelia
- **Population:** Michoacán state population was approximately 992,000 in 1910 (national census). Nueva Italia itself was a small colony of a few hundred in the early 1900s.
- **Economy:** Tropical agriculture (citrus, sugarcane, rice) — planned hacienda colony
- **Language of records:** Spanish
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration in many Tierra Caliente communities; Cristero War (1926–1929) further affected church records

## Boundary changes
- Nueva Italia was part of **Parácuaro municipality** from its founding (~1903) until February 12, 1942, when Múgica municipality was created and absorbed the town. All civil registry records for events at Nueva Italia before 1942 were filed under Parácuaro.
- Gabriel Zamora municipality was created November 7, 1955 — not relevant for 1880–1930 records.
- FamilySearch wiki for Múgica states explicitly: **"There are no records available online for the municipality of Múgica"** (civil registration, church records, and census). ([Múgica Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/M%C3%BAgica,_Infiernillo,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy))

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration was instituted nationally at the municipal level in 1859; by 1867 most areas were keeping records per the [Mexico Getting Started](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Getting_Started) wiki page
- **Registered under:** Parácuaro municipality (1880–1942); filing office: Registro Civil de Parácuaro
- **What exists on FamilySearch:** FamilySearch has **193 digitized volumes** for Parácuaro in the target period. The first page of 50 results shows:
  - *Nacimientos (Births)*: volumes confirmed for 1917–1930 (some 1926–1930 volumes have 0 images — not yet scanned). **No birth volumes for years 1910–1916 appeared in the first 50 results**; 193 total volumes exist, so earlier birth records may appear on pages 2–4 — this must be confirmed by direct catalog search
  - *Matrimonios (Marriages)*: volumes for 1881–1930, all 100% name-indexed
  - *Defunciones (Deaths)*: volumes for 1881–1930, all 100% name-indexed
- **Digitization level:** **Indexed + images** — all Parácuaro volumes returned are 100% recordSearchablePercent (name-searchable via `record_search`), fulltextSearchable: false (images must be viewed directly)
- **Indexed collection:** [Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243) (CID 1916243) — index & images; this is the searchable front-end for the Parácuaro volumes and should be searched by name first
- **Ancestry parallel:** Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births 1859–1934 at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/) — index & images ($)
- **Gaps:** Birth records for 1910–1916 are possibly absent from the digitized set or not on the first page; Revolution-era disruption (1910–1920) may have caused lapses in civil registration. Volumes for 1926–1930 births have 0 images — catalogued but not yet scanned.

### Church records
- **Primary denomination:** Roman Catholic; Arquidiócesis de Morelia
- **Note on Nueva Italia:** As a new colony (c. 1903), Nueva Italia likely lacked its own parish in 1910. Residents would have baptized children at the nearest established parish — most likely in Parácuaro or Apatzingán
- **Digitized collection:** [Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1883388) (CID 1883388) — **index only**; coverage varies by parish. The wiki for this collection states coverage is 1549–1909, making it the key resource for pre-1910 baptisms and pre-1910 marriages. Baptism records would include date/place of birth, parents' names, and godparents.
- **Ancestry parallel:** [Michoacán, Mexico, Catholic Church Records, 1649–1909](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60021) — images only ($)
- **Broader index collections:**
  - [Mexico Baptisms, 1560–1950](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1473011) — index only; coverage varies
  - [Mexico Marriages, 1570–1950](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1473012) — index only
  - [Mexico Deaths, 1680–1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1473013) — index only
- **Language:** Spanish; records are handwritten in narrative style
- **Archdiocese volumes (browse-only):** FamilySearch has multiple volumes of Arquidiócesis de Morelia marriage information records (Información matrimonial), many covering 1880–1909, at 100% indexed. Parish-level baptism volumes exist for some Tierra Caliente parishes (e.g., Churumuco baptisms 1862–1880, Peribán baptisms 1876–1922)
- **Research tip:** To browse church records directly, navigate via [Collection Browse Page](https://familysearch.org/search/image/index#uri=https://familysearch.org/recapi/sord/collection/1883388/waypoints) → City or Town → Parish → Record Type and Years

### Census records
- **1930 National Census:** [Mexico National Census, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1307314) — **indexed + images**; also at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1771) ($). This is the most important census for research in the 1910–1930 period. If Mauro Cruz Corona was born c. 1910 he would appear as approximately age 20 in 1930 and may list parents or birth place.
- **Earlier censuses:** No nationally accessible census from 1895, 1900, or 1910 is indexed online for Michoacán per the wiki. Mexico Census history can be reviewed at [Mexico Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Census)
- **No records available online** for any Múgica municipality census (per FS wiki)

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills (testamentos), intestate administrations, guardianships — held at the municipal and state level
- **Where held:** State archives (Morelia) and local archives; 63 archives in 55 municipalities per [Michoacán Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy#Repositories) page
- **Access:** Likely physical only; not indexed online for this period

### Land records
- **Types:** Property tax records, land grants, hacienda records
- **Note:** Nueva Italia was founded on hacienda lands (the Cusi family). Hacienda administrative records may name workers and their families. Mexico land and property guidance at [Mexico Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Land_and_Property)
- **Access:** Physical; state or national archives

### Military records
- **Relevant conflict:** Mexican Revolution 1910–1920; Cristero War 1926–1929
- **Types:** Draft records, service records
- **Where held:** Dirección General de Archivo e Historia (Sedena) — [gob.mx](https://www.gob.mx/sedena/acciones-y-programas/expedicion-de-documentos); Archivo General de la Nación, Mexico City — [agn.gob.mx](http://www.agn.gob.mx/)

### Cemetery records
- **Panteón Municipal de Nueva Italia**, address: Vicente Villada #0, Reforma, Múgica (per FS wiki)
- **Panteón Ejidal de Gámbara**, address: Calle Aldama, Gámbara, Múgica

- **Borders:** Michoacán's Tierra Caliente borders Guerrero to the south and Jalisco/Colima to the west. If the family had Guerrero origins, check that state's records as well.
